5 signs your business has outgrown its systems:

1. You type the same information into more than one system.
2. Month-end means days of spreadsheets.
3. Only one person knows how it all works.
4. You can't see how you're performing without asking someone.
5. Your systems don't talk to each other.

If you recognised two or more, you're in good company. Many established businesses have systems that grew piece by piece, and the people who set them up have often moved on.

title: Tech jargon, in plain English
images: p06-jargon-01.png | p06-jargon-02.png | p06-jargon-03.png | p06-jargon-04.png | p06-jargon-05.png | p06-jargon-06.png
linkedin_caption:
Tech jargon, in plain English.

CRM: a single, organised record of every customer and enquiry, so nothing slips through the cracks.
POS: the till and card payment system, connected to your stock and accounts so every sale is recorded once.
Automation: getting your systems to pass information to each other on their own, so nobody types the same thing twice.
Cloud: your software and data stored online rather than on one machine in the back office.

If a supplier ever uses a term you don't understand, ask them to explain it in plain English. A good one always can.

title: What does digital transformation mean?
linkedin_caption:
What does "digital transformation" actually mean?

Strip away the jargon and it's this: using modern technology to make your business easier to run.

- Less re-typing and fewer mistakes.
- Numbers you can see and trust.
- A business that doesn't depend on one person's memory.

It isn't about buying the newest thing. It's about fixing the right things in the right order, without disrupting the day-to-day.

title: If your main computer failed tomorrow
linkedin_caption:
A simple question for business owners:

If your main computer failed tomorrow, would you know where your data is?

Plenty of established businesses aren't sure. Files live on one machine, passwords are shared, and nobody has checked whether the backup actually works.

Security and backup are part of every project we deliver, and every systems audit checks both: sign-ins, who has access to what, and whether your data is safely backed up.
